## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Double-blind: "authors do not know the identity of the reviewers and reviewers do not know the identity of the authors" (paraphrase of AOM support article https://support.aom.org/hc/en-us/articles/360059745573-What-is-the-review-process-at-AMR-Are-submissions-blind-reviewed-When-will-I-hear-back-about-my-submission, read 2026-11-23). Flow stated there: the editor screens, assigns an associate editor, the associate editor screens again and invites reviewers, usually three per manuscript; the associate editor makes the decision on revise or reject. Authors submit a Word file with title page and author-identifying references removed (https://www.aom.org/publications/journals/publishing-with-aom/author-and-reviewer-resources/author-resources/submitting-to-review/) |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. No transfer policy found on the pages read |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Blank. No statement found |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | Blank. No source found |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Authors may request reviewers and associate editors in an optional cover letter, but requests are not always honoured; two associate editors must be chosen in the submission system (https://support.aom.org/hc/en-us/articles/360059746253-Do-I-need-to-include-a-cover-letter-with-my-submission-Can-I-request-reviewers-and-or-an-associate-editor, read 2026-11-23). The same article calls cover letters optional while the AI policy asks for AI-use disclosure in the cover letter (see AI Policy); the pages were not reconciled |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | Publisher-wide, repeated on the AMR submitting page: work must be created by the authors and not be the product of AI tools unless appropriate to the research question and properly cited; AI use is disclosed in the cover letter and in the acknowledgements, and authors confirm they have read the AOM AI policy (https://www.aom.org/publications/journals/publishing-with-aom/author-and-reviewer-resources/author-resources/submitting-to-review/, read 2026-11-23) |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | No gate found. Use is permitted with a two-step report: disclosure per research stage (conceptualization, design, data preparation and analysis, presentation of results, writing and editing) and confirmation that outputs were reviewed and verified |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 (allowed with mandatory stage-by-stage disclosure and accountability confirmation; same rubric as the Mind entry) |
| **Summary** | AOM policy page (https://www.aom.org/publications/journals/publishing-with-aom/aom-artificial-intelligence-policy/, read 2026-11-23): authors may use AI tools but AI cannot replace human judgment or accountability; authors disclose per research stage and confirm verification; editors may ask for details; language-model use is cited following the Chicago Manual of Style; undisclosed use in published articles leads to corrective action. Reviewers must not upload any part of a manuscript into an AI tool and must not use AI to generate review reports; editors must not share submitted manuscripts with generative AI |
| **Source URL** | https://www.aom.org/publications/journals/publishing-with-aom/aom-artificial-intelligence-policy/ ; https://www.aom.org/publications/journals/publishing-with-aom/author-and-reviewer-resources/author-resources/submitting-to-review/ |

### Preprint Policy

> Two AOM pages read on 2026-11-23 differ and are both recorded. The Open Access page (https://www.aom.org/publications/journals/publishing-with-aom/open-access/) says preprints can be shared anywhere at any time and adds "Peer review restrictions apply". The AMR submitting page (https://www.aom.org/publications/journals/publishing-with-aom/author-and-reviewer-resources/author-resources/submitting-to-review/) says working papers, drafts or final versions of a submitted manuscript posted on a website should be taken down during the review process, while a conference paper or a paper in the AOM Annual Meeting Proceedings may still be submitted.

| Stage | Allowed? | Notes |
|-------|----------|-------|
| Pre-submission | Yes per the Open Access page; see the conflict note above | The AMR page asks that postings be removed during review |
| Under review | No per the AMR submitting page (postings taken down during review) | The paper may not be under review elsewhere |
| Post-acceptance (AAM) | Partly | Accepted manuscripts can be shared privately and on personal websites or blogs; public posting on an institutional repository only after a 12-month embargo (Open Access page above). Embargo: 12 months |
| Version of Record | Not freely shareable | Complete open access to the Version of Record, including an institutional repository, only after the 12-month embargo; AOM keeps copyright |

## Format

> Sources: the AMR submitting page and the AOM-wide editorial style guide listed under Identity, read 2026-11-23, plus the AMR support articles cited per row.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Conceptual and theoretical articles; formal theory (including simulations and other computational or mathematical modelling) is accepted on the same criteria (https://support.aom.org/hc/en-us/articles/360059744013-Does-AMR-publish-papers-using-formal-theory). The support article on literature reviews and case studies says AMR does not publish literature reviews, case studies or manuscripts with empirical data (https://support.aom.org/hc/en-us/articles/360059743913-Does-AMR-publish-literature-reviews-or-case-studies). OpenAlex types of the 263 records dated 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23: 259 articles and 4 editorials (retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Word limit** | No word limit stated. Page guide: initial submissions should not exceed 30 double-spaced pages excluding references, tables and figures (https://www.aom.org/publications/journals/publishing-with-aom/author-and-reviewer-resources/author-resources/submitting-to-review/); a support article says about 25 to 30 double-spaced pages (https://support.aom.org/hc/en-us/articles/360059744573-What-are-the-page-limits-for-submissions-How-do-I-format-my-submission-correctly). The journal assesses a contribution-to-length ratio |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Blank. The pages call 30 pages a general guide and say shorter submissions meet the same standards; no statement on exceptions |
| **Abstract limit** | No more than 200 words, placed with the title on page 2 (AOM style guide, https://www.aom.org/publications/journals/publishing-with-aom/author-and-reviewer-resources/author-resources/author-resources-editorial-style-guides/, read 2026-11-23). Keywords: not stated on the pages read |
| **Reference limit** | No cap found; references are excluded from the 30-page guide. Style: the AOM guide (author-year in text, alphabetical list, unnumbered entries) |
| **Supplementary material** | Appendices and supplementary material go last in the manuscript file (AOM style guide above); no separate online-supplement rule found |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit found. Tables first, then figures, after the references (AOM style guide above). Formal propositions and boxes-and-arrows figures are not required (https://support.aom.org/hc/en-us/articles/360057905854--Does-my-paper-need-propositions-and-figures-with-boxes-and-arrows) |
| **Style / submission format** | Word file; Times New Roman 12 point; Letter size; double-spaced body; 1-inch margins; no page numbers or running heads; footnotes rather than endnotes; three heading levels, unnumbered (AOM style guide above). Submitted through ScholarOne ("Manuscript Central"); submission is allowed once per paper, and a significantly overlapping paper cannot be resubmitted (AMR submitting page); papers cannot be under review elsewhere |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** A theoretical contribution is the stated requirement: submissions must extend theory in ways that develop testable knowledge-based claims, by new theory, challenge or clarification of existing theory, synthesis into fresh theory, or defining a novel theoretical problem (https://www.aom.org/research/journals/review, read 2026-11-23).
- **What kind of engagement?** Contribution to management theory that is accessible to a broad management audience: the same two criteria apply to formal theory papers, and papers that only formalize existing theory or mainly advance formal technique are described as unlikely to be published (https://support.aom.org/hc/en-us/articles/360059744013-Does-AMR-publish-papers-using-formal-theory, read 2026-11-23). The submitting page says a contribution-to-length ratio is assessed and research implications must be presented explicitly (https://www.aom.org/publications/journals/publishing-with-aom/author-and-reviewer-resources/author-resources/submitting-to-review/).
- **Article type and length**: conceptual articles; about 25 to 30 double-spaced pages excluding references, tables and figures (support article https://support.aom.org/hc/en-us/articles/360059744573-What-are-the-page-limits-for-submissions-How-do-I-format-my-submission-correctly). Formal propositions are not required (https://support.aom.org/hc/en-us/articles/360057905854--Does-my-paper-need-propositions-and-figures-with-boxes-and-arrows).
- **Special-issue framing seen**: Special Topic Forums are mentioned in https://support.aom.org/hc/en-us/articles/360059745573-What-is-the-review-process-at-AMR-Are-submissions-blind-reviewed-When-will-I-hear-back-about-my-submission ; no current AMR call text was read.
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Empirical or literature-review submissions are outside the stated scope (https://support.aom.org/hc/en-us/articles/360059743913-Does-AMR-publish-literature-reviews-or-case-studies). The AOM author-resources page says some manuscripts are declined with only a general statement and cannot be appealed (https://www.aom.org/publications/journals/publishing-with-aom/author-and-reviewer-resources/author-resources/). No desk-rejection data exists (SciRev 0 reviews: https://scirev.org/reviews/academy-of-management-review/).

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts are records of this source dated 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23 (OpenAlex: 263 records, 172 with an abstract) whose title or abstract matches the regex in the keyword table (AI-Research Notes); shares use the 172 abstract records as denominator. Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement. Scores measure how often a method appears, not how a reviewer would judge it.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 0 | The journal states it does not publish manuscripts with empirical data (https://support.aom.org/hc/en-us/articles/360059743913-Does-AMR-publish-literature-reviews-or-case-studies). Counts: survey, questionnaire, experiment or quantitative terms 4 of 172 (2.3%); the count rule alone would give 2, and the editorial statement overrides it to 0 (the four hits were not inspected individually) |
| Qualitative interviews | 0 | Same editorial statement; "interview" 0 and "qualitative" 0 of 172 abstract records |
| Autoethnography | 0 | "autoethnograph" 0 of 172; case studies are stated as not published (support article above) |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 5 | Editorial statements: mission text says the journal publishes theoretical insights (https://www.aom.org/research/journals/review) and the submitting page calls it a theory development journal publishing conceptual articles (https://www.aom.org/publications/journals/publishing-with-aom/author-and-reviewer-resources/author-resources/submitting-to-review/). Counts: "theoretical" 52 (30.2%), "conceptual" 38 (22.1%) |
| Mixed methods | 0 | "mixed methods" 0 of 172 |
| Meta-analysis / systematic review | 0 | "meta-analysis" 0 and "systematic review" 0 of 172; the support article says literature reviews are not published (URL above). "review|synthesis" matches 9 abstracts (5.2%); these hits were not inspected individually |
| Formal theory / simulation (added row) | 2 | Count: simulation, agent-based, formal or mathematical or computational model terms 8 of 172 (4.7%), which gives 2 by the count rule. Editorial statement (recorded, not used to raise the score): formal theory including simulations and mathematical models is accepted on the same criteria (https://support.aom.org/hc/en-us/articles/360059744013-Does-AMR-publish-papers-using-formal-theory) |

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

Reviewer behaviour itself is not observable from public pages; what follows is what public pages do show.

| Aspect | Detail | Evidence |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Dominant tradition** | Editorial-team page (https://www.aom.org/publications/journals/review/review-editorial-team/, read 2026-11-23) has 117 person cards: 1 Editor, 18 Associate Editors, 1 Senior Managing Editor, 95 Editorial Review Board members, and 2 cards with no role label (one with the role slot empty, one with an affiliation printed in the role slot) (117 = 1+18+1+95+2). The Editor's bio lists organizational behaviour, social information processing, creativity and workplace diversity among her interests; the associate editors' bios name fields such as entrepreneurship, strategy, organizational behaviour and international business (bios on the same page). Reviewers are drawn from board members and a database of ad hoc reviewers (support article, URL below) | https://www.aom.org/publications/journals/review/review-editorial-team/ ; https://support.aom.org/hc/en-us/articles/360059745573-What-is-the-review-process-at-AMR-Are-submissions-blind-reviewed-When-will-I-hear-back-about-my-submission |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | Blank. AMR does not take empirical data per its own support article (https://support.aom.org/hc/en-us/articles/360059743913-Does-AMR-publish-literature-reviews-or-case-studies), and no human-subjects rule was found on the AMR submitting page; the AOM Code of Ethics (linked from https://www.aom.org/publications/journals/publishing-with-aom/author-and-reviewer-resources/author-resources/) was not read |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author papers appear: 47 of 259 article records in the window (18.1%; OpenAlex, retrieved 2026-11-23). AOM says authorship is determined at initial submission and can change before acceptance with written approval of all listed authors (https://www.aom.org/publications/journals/publishing-with-aom/author-and-reviewer-resources/author-resources/) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | No independent-scholar rule found on the pages read. The title page is anonymised for review; affiliations are asked only for accepted papers (AOM style guide, https://www.aom.org/publications/journals/publishing-with-aom/author-and-reviewer-resources/author-resources/author-resources-editorial-style-guides/). Whether independent authors appear among published authors was not measured |
| **Data transparency requirement** | None found: the AMR submitting page and the AOM author-resources page contain no data-sharing section (searched the page text for "data": only cookie-banner and an unrelated journal blurb matched) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Double-blind: the submitted Word file must have the title page and all author-identifying references removed; acknowledgements go in the cover letter (https://www.aom.org/publications/journals/publishing-with-aom/author-and-reviewer-resources/author-resources/submitting-to-review/). Drafts posted on websites should be taken down during review (same page), which conflicts with the Open Access page's preprint wording (see Preprint Policy) |
| **AI use** | Disclosure required per research stage, in the cover letter and acknowledgements (https://www.aom.org/publications/journals/publishing-with-aom/aom-artificial-intelligence-policy/) |
| **Open access and cost** | No Gold route and no APC route (https://www.aom.org/publications/journals/publishing-with-aom/open-access/); OpenAlex shows 76 of 263 records as green OA (retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Originality screening** | AOM checks all submissions for plagiarism with Crossref iThenticate (https://www.aom.org/publications/journals/publishing-with-aom/author-and-reviewer-resources/author-resources/, read 2026-11-23). Reciprocity: authors are expected to review for AMR if asked (AMR submitting page). Appeals: some declinations are final; formal appeals go through the AOM ethics resources (author-resources page) |

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Empirical or review content**: the journal states it does not publish literature reviews, case studies or manuscripts with empirical data (Methodological Preferences, support article 360059743913). An empirical manuscript is outside the stated scope.
- **Prior review at AMR**: a previously reviewed and rejected paper cannot be resubmitted unless it has a different theoretical framing and a substantially different question (Framing Requirements, support article 360059746313; AMR submitting page).
- **Concurrent submission and postings**: the paper cannot be under review elsewhere, and posted drafts should be taken down during review (Preprint Policy, AMR submitting page).
- **Anonymised Word file and AI disclosure**: title page and author-identifying references removed; AI use disclosed per research stage (Peer Review, AI Policy).
- No other hard blocker is supported by a fact I could read.

### Soft Tax

- **Length**: the guide is 30 double-spaced pages excluding references, tables and figures (Format); the journal assesses a contribution-to-length ratio, and no fixed word limit exists.
- **Reciprocity**: authors are expected to review for AMR if asked (Originality screening row, Practical Concerns).
- **Time**: the stated goal is a decision within 60 days; no measured figure exists (Review Cycle Time).
- **Open access**: no Gold route; the Version of Record may be made openly available only after 12 months (Preprint Policy, Open Access).
- **Conflicting preprint wording**: two AOM pages differ (Preprint Policy); an author who posts a preprint should confirm with the editorial office first.

### Best Suited For

- Conceptual and theory-building manuscripts for a broad management audience: "theoretical" in 30.2% and "conceptual" in 22.1% of abstract records, and the mission text asks for theory extension (Orientation).
- Formal-theory or simulation papers whose contribution is to management theory rather than to technique (Methodological Preferences, formal-theory support article).
- Work on organizations and artificial intelligence, paradox, stakeholders or institutions: these are the most frequent or most cited themes in the window (Epistemological & Political Leanings).
- First-person, active-voice writing: the AOM style guide asks for it and 163 of 172 abstract records use it (Voice & Style).

### Not Recommended For

- Empirical papers, case studies and literature reviews: stated as not published (Methodological Preferences); counts for survey, interview or qualitative terms are 0 to 4 of 172.
- Authors needing a verified turnaround figure: only a stated 60-day goal exists and no first-hand report exists (Review Cycle Time).
- Authors who need Gold open access: AOM does not offer it (Open Access).
- Work centred on decolonial, Indigenous or non-Western framing as the main contribution: 0 of 172 abstracts match (Sensitive Topics); this shows absence in the window, not a stated policy.

### Rejection Fallback Chain

> No source states where rejected authors usually go. The rows below are topical neighbours that already exist in this corpus, listed only because they share the subject area (organization and management theory); they are not a claim about acceptance odds.

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |

| 2 | [Journal of Management Studies](journal-of-management-studies.md) | Same broad subject area; an entry exists in this corpus. No fit evidence collected here |
